findings.reason: §2's scope, tests and negative control should hoist the `dispatch.py:274-283` resolve-move idiom into the one owner and make all three callers use it, rather than add a parallel `release_waiters` path whose existence depends on a premise the code refutes.
findings.text: §1 asserts "the only call that moves a request from `awaiting-upstream` to `queued` is the release step inside `admit_once`", but the primitive has three call sites: `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:274` (`_queue_validated_waits`, which already does resolve → `_move_pointer` → phase at queue time), `reckon/crew/runs.py:2146` (the drain view resolving an overdue `awaiting-upstream` to decide `stuck`), and `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:2282` (inside `admit_once`), with `move_queued_run` at `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:324`. §2 therefore designs a fourth entry point to a primitive that already has two non-pass callers, and the plan's own cause for nova's 41-minute wait is unproven as stated

findings.reason: §8 should name the existing parser as the thing `crew complete --land` is routed through, and drop or re-scope the arms that assert behaviour `land_once` already provides, otherwise the node re-implements a working guard and its negative control cannot fail.
findings.text: §8 is written as though both manifest-commit behaviours are absent, but `_delivered_revision` (`reckon/crew/queue_landing.py:28`) already parses an entry that leads with a revision and carries a subject, or a bare list of several revisions, and `_unreadable_entry_guard` (`reckon/crew/queue_landing.py:52`) already records a refusal, with the entry quoted, for a manifest whose last entry names no revision — landed and exercised by `tests/test_the_landing_pass_measures_and_lands.py`; the residual defect is confined to the `crew complete --land` subprocess re-reading the manifest on its own

findings.reason: each instance is a forked owner that will drift from the original, and (b) and (c) additionally put a deliverable outside the write paths that were supposed to produce it; naming `resumption.py`, `process_liveness.py`, `needs_you.py` and `obligations.py` in the write paths is a one-line change per section now and a stranded node later.
findings.text: three sections each place a mechanism beside its existing owner, and the plan names none of them. (a) §2 adds `release_waiters` without naming `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:274` or `reckon/crew/runs.py:2146`, the two callers that already release a waiter outside a pass. (b) §6 names `reckon/crew/recovery_wait.py` as the write path for dead-park classification, but that module validates wait-probe *shape* and its own docstring at `reckon/crew/recovery_wait.py:474-489` says the reader that decides whether a park lifts is `reckon/crew/resumption.py:1776 sweep`, while process liveness is owned by `reckon/crew/process_liveness.py:13 process_alive` and `reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:419 _live_descendant` — so "three sweeps unchanged and no live process" written into `recovery_wait.py` duplicates two owners and lands in the wrong file. (c) §7 names `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py` and `reckon/crew/runs.py` for "the obligations view shows the stall … once, until it clears", but the obligations view and its stall machinery are `reckon/crew/needs_you.py:134` (stall_seconds, `stall_stream_path`, `needs_you_rows`) with `reckon/crew/obligations.py` — both are outside the section's declared write paths, so the node cannot deliver the third arm at all

findings.reason: an unspecified fit query will either duplicate `_fit` or silently disagree with it about a window, which is exactly the failure the plan's own §1 case records ("no other lane was tried"); the section must say which picker entry point it calls.
findings.text: §5 adds a context-fit query to the admission pass ("asks the picker for a lane whose context window fits the node's estimate, among the lanes the request's session may use under the lifts in force") without justifying why the picker's existing per-candidate verdict cannot be extended: `_fit` (`reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:663`) already runs the competence check for every candidate backend and returns its reasons, and `move_queued_run` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:324`) already re-composes a launch on another backend, so the honest change is to ask the picker for its ranked candidates and take the first whose competence verdict passes, not to re-derive fitness in the admission pass

findings.reason: each section must either name the public definition, CLI option or refusal it retires or merges, or state in its own text why nothing can be, which is a one-line addition per section and the only thing that keeps the fourth figure from growing in three families at once.
findings.text: at public_definitions 2271, cli_options 441, mcp_views 31 and refusal_families 23, four sections add surface with no retirement stated in their own text: §2 (`:65`) adds `queue_admission.release_waiters` to the public definitions, §3 (`:78`) adds the `crew land` verb with a `--watch` option to the CLI surface, §5 (`:101`) adds two refusal messages at `crew queue edit` (context fit, live claim), and §7 (`:124`) adds a stall verdict kind, a drain-view age field and an obligations row

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §2's `release_waiters`, §3's `queue_landing` loop and §4's digest-keyed memo each hide several steps (wait resolution, dead-section rule, readiness read, pointer move; per-tick action selection, own lock, bounded `srun`; blob+identity keyed coverage) behind one call each, which is the shape asked for.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan adds three parallel owners over mechanisms that already have one: wait release beside `dispatch.py:274`/`runs.py:2146`, dead-park classification outside `reckon/crew/resumption.py:1776`, and stall-obligation display outside `reckon/crew/needs_you.py:134`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 2271, cli_options 441, mcp_views 31, refusal_families 23; §2, §3, §5 and §7 each add to one of these families (`release_waiters`, `crew land --watch`, two edit-time refusals, a stall verdict plus a drain-view field plus an obligations row) and none names what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's causal premise that release happens only inside `admit_once` is wrong: `resolve_waits` is already called from three sites (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:274`, `reckon/crew/runs.py:2146`, `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:2282`), and two of §8's three behaviours already exist in `reckon/crew/queue_landing.py:28` and `:52`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §5 asks the picker for "a lane whose context window fits", a second fit query beside the picker's own per-candidate competence verdict in `reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:663`, without saying why that candidate ranking cannot be extended.
